name: XDOF
summary: XDOF builds teleoperation-data pipelines and annotation systems for training general-purpose robots. It raised $70 million in June 2026, while a later $1.2 billion valuation was only reported as financing talks.
overview: XDOF builds data pipelines, collection tools and annotation systems for training general-purpose robots. TechCrunch reported a $70M Series A in June 2026; later reporting of a $1.2B valuation described financing talks, not a completed round.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: TechCrunch reported the Series A; later $1.2B Series B valuation context was financing talks, not a completed round.

bull_case: High-quality real-world data is a bottleneck for general-purpose robotics. A scaled collection and annotation network could become critical infrastructure for robotics labs and manufacturers.
bear_case: The Series B terms were not final and the $1.2B valuation remains reported talks, not a completed transaction. Data collection is operationally demanding and competition can intensify as robotics spending rises.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: Robotics-data infrastructure using teleoperation, collection and annotation systems.
company: XDOF builds data pipelines, collection tools and annotation systems for training general-purpose robots. Its founders, UC Berkeley researchers Philipp Wu and Fred Shentu, developed the GELLO teleoperation system for generating robot-training data.

TechCrunch reported a $70M Series A in June 2026 and said annualized revenue was approaching $50M with 20 customers, including frontier AI labs. It separately reported that a Series B at about $1.2B was under discussion, not final.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Robotics needs real-world training data that the internet cannot supply. XDOF is positioned as a data-supply-chain provider for physical AI, where collection quality and operational scale may be more valuable than a single robot product.

changed.text: Profile reviewed against available public information.

takeaways: XDOF collects and annotates real-world data for general-purpose robotics training.
TechCrunch reported a $70M Series A in June 2026.
A $1.2B valuation was reported in Series B talks, not a completed financing.
